Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, MoS for Power and New & Renewable Energy, leads Indian delegation to Singapore International Energy Week 2026
articles.full_content:
Holds bilateral meetings with Singapore, Bhutan, IRENA and IEA on the sidelines
The Union Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, led the Indian delegation to the Singapore International Energy Week (SIEW) 2026, held at the Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention Centre, Singapore, from 26th to 28th October 2026.
SIEW 2026 coincided with the 25th year of Singapore's Energy Market Authority. The Summit was expanded into a two-day event this year and featured the Singapore-IEA Forum, the Singapore-IRENA Forum, and the IAEA at SIEW. Shri Naik participated and delivered a keynote on Day 1 and the Opening Remarks for the 2nd day of the event.
Addressing sessions on the first two days of the event, Shri Naik said India’s installed electricity capacity stood at 558.9 GW as of 30 September 2026, of which about 308 GW, or 55 per cent, came from non-fossil sources. He noted that India achieved 50 per cent non-fossil installed capacity in June 2025, five years ahead of its 2030 NDC target, and is now working towards 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030. Highlighting progress under the flagship schemes, he said that around 53 lakh rooftop solar systems had been installed under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, benefiting about 63 lakh households. Under PM-KUSUM, nearly 12 lakh standalone solar pumps have been installed, and more than 17 lakh grid-connected agricultural pumps have been solarised, adding about 16.7 GW of decentralised renewable energy capacity and benefiting around 30 lakh farmers.
Shri Naik also held bilateral meetings with the following countries/organisations on the sidelines of SIEW 2026:
Singapore : Shri Naik met Ms Gan Siow Huang, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Energy and Trade and Industry, Republic of Singapore. The two sides discussed energy cooperation under the India-Singapore Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including the proposed cross-border electricity interconnection between the two countries. Shri Naik invited long-term Singaporean investment in transmission, pumped storage, battery storage and renewable energy in India. Cooperation in green hydrogen and ammonia, energy efficiency, and partnerships between Indian power equipment manufacturers and Singapore's utilities was also discussed.
Bhutan : Shri Naik met H.E. Lyonpo Sonam Tashi, Minister for Energy and Natural Resources, Royal Government of Bhutan, and congratulated him on assuming office. The two Ministers reviewed progress on the 1200 MW Punatsangchhu-I Hydroelectric Project, where dam works have progressed steadily since concreting resumed in April 2026, and noted the satisfactory operations of the 1020 MW Punatsangchhu-II project. They also discussed the other projects that are under discussion in partnership with Indian entities, along with the cross-border transmission planning up to 2040.
IRENA : Shri Naik met Mr Francesco La Camera, Director-General, International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA). He appreciated IR

SIEW 2026 coincided with the 25th year of Singapore's Energy Market Authority. The Summit was expanded into a two-day event this year and featured the Singapore-IEA Forum, the Singapore-IRENA Forum, and the IAEA at SIEW.

Green Hydrogen
articles.full_content:
Emerging Pillar of India’s Clean Energy Transition
Green hydrogen is emerging as a pillar of India’s clean energy transition. It is produced by splitting water using renewable electricity. It can help reduce emissions in sectors such as fertiliser production, petroleum refining, iron and steel manufacturing, heavy-duty road transport and shipping . The National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM) supports domestic manufacturing, production, assured demand and credible certification. From green ammonia auctions to India’s first hydrogen train, early projects point to a promising path.
Why Green Hydrogen
Hydrogen is an energy carrier that stores energy and delivers it for varied uses. In a fuel cell, it reacts with oxygen to produce electricity, leaving only water and heat as by-products, and no polluting compounds or greenhouse gases. Although pure hydrogen is not found in large quantities in nature, it can be extracted from compounds such as water or natural gas. Its environmental impact therefore depends on how it is made. Conventional methods rely on fossil fuels and release carbon emissions.
Production using renewable electricity from solar and wind power can cut this footprint substantially. Hydrogen made by splitting water using renewable power is called green hydrogen . Unlike fossil-based routes, this process emits far less carbon. India’s abundant solar and wind resources make domestic production feasible. This diversifies the country’s energy sources and strengthens energy security. It also supports India’s goal of net-zero emissions by 2070.
Green hydrogen matters most in sectors where cutting emissions is difficult. Reasons include high-temperature heat needs, chemical processes and few alternatives to fossil fuels. These hard-to-abate sectors include fertiliser, petroleum refining, iron and steel, heavy-duty road transport and shipping. Fertiliser and refining plants already use hydrogen, so green hydrogen can replace the fossil-based supply. It can also support lower-emission steelmaking, selected transport uses and energy storage. It is especially useful where direct electrification is difficult or less practical.
For India, wider adoption could reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels. It would also lessen exposure to global fuel price swings. The sector could open opportunities in manufacturing, draw investment, create jobs and expand exports. Building capabilities across the value chain would strengthen domestic supply chains and spur industrial innovation. Green hydrogen can thus support self-reliance, sustainable industrial growth and a low-carbon future.
What Makes Hydrogen “Green”
Hydrogen releases no carbon dioxide when used, so its climate impact depends on how it is produced. In August 2023, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) notified India’s Green Hydrogen Standard. The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, has driven a sustained shift from a permission-based to a trust-based regulatory framework. Reforms across the startup ecosystem, compliance reduction, sectoral regulation, foreign direct investment and single-window clearances have reduced the regulatory burden on businesses and delivered measurable outcomes in business entry, employment, investment and digital service delivery.
DPIIT has recognised 2,50,046 startups, reporting over 25.42 lakh jobs across 770+ districts and 56 industries. Of these startups, 52% are from non-metro cities and 48% have at least one woman director. Annual recognitions increased from 34,200 in FY 2023-24 to 36,440 in FY 2024-25.
Under the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme, ₹775.67 crore has been approved for 4,194 startups across 32 States/UTs through 244 incubators, including 2,147 women-led startups and 2,356 startups from Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Under the Fund of Funds for Startups, SIDBI has committed ₹12,623 crore to 166 Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), which have invested ₹28,254 crore in 1,475 startups.
The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups has guaranteed 532 loans worth ₹1,662.71 crore to startups employing 41,637 people. The guarantee cover per borrower has been doubled from ₹10 crore to ₹20 crore, while the annual fee has been reduced to 1% for 27 Champion Sectors.
A total of 63 regulatory reforms have been enabled, including the abolition of angel tax, harmonisation of long-term capital gains taxation for listed and unlisted shares, and permission for insurance companies, EPFO, superannuation funds and gratuity funds to invest in AIFs. Further, 4,467 startups hold the Section 80-IAC certificate of eligibility.
With prior-experience, prior-turnover and Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) requirements relaxed, the number of startups registered on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) has increased from 7,929 in January 2021 to 43,260. These startups have delivered 6.23 lakh orders worth ₹68,105 crore to public buyers. Dedicated startup policies have expanded from four States/UTs in 2016 to 32. In addition, 104 new incubators have been established across 17 States/UTs, while the TEJAS initiative covers 132 districts in 27 States/UTs.

DPIIT Launches 6th Edition of National Startup Awards to Recognise Innovation and Entrepreneurship

National Startup Awards 6.0 to Recognise Startups Across 20 Sectoral and 3 Special Categories, Introduces 12 New Sectors National Startup Awards 6.0 Introduces Student Innovator Award, Offers ₹25 Lakh Cash Prize Across Eligible Categories Applications for National Startup Awards 6.0 Open from 27 October to 20 November 2026
The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, has launched the 6th Edition of the National Startup Awards (NSA 6.0) under the Startup India initiative to recognise innovation and entrepreneurship and strengthen India’s startup ecosystem.
The year 2026 marks the completion of ten years of the Startup India initiative, launched in January 2016 to build a strong, inclusive and innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem in the country. Since its inception in 2019, the National Startup Awards have emerged as a flagship initiative under Startup India, providing a national platform to recognise entrepreneurial excellence and showcase innovative solutions addressing critical challenges across sectors.
The National Startup Awards recognise startups demonstrating outstanding performance in innovation, scalability, sustainability and socio-economic impact. Building upon the success of the previous five editions, NSA 6.0 seeks to strengthen India’s startup ecosystem by encouraging innovation-led entrepreneurship, fostering inclusive participation and promoting globally competitive startups.
NSA 6.0 will recognise innovation, entrepreneurship and excellence across 20 sectoral categories and three special award categories, reflecting India’s evolving startup ecosystem, emerging technologies and national development priorities. This edition introduces 12 new sectoral categories: Biomanufacturing; Consumer Industries; Defence & Security; Rural Economy, Traditional Industries & Livelihoods; Education & Skilling; Electronics, Semiconductors & Advanced Manufacturing; Sports, Fitness & Sports-Tech; Future Mobility & Automotive; Ocean & Blue Economy; Space-Tech, Drones & Aerospace; Telecom, Connectivity & Digital Infrastructure; and Travel, Tourism & Hospitality.
The three special award categories are Women-Led Startup of the Year, North-East Startup Excellence and the newly introduced Student Innovator / Aspiring Entrepreneur Award. Introduced for the first time, the student award aims to foster a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship among school and college students across all 36 States and Union Territories. It marks a step towards nurturing the next generation of innovators and entrepreneurs and expanding the reach of the National Startup Awards.
Winning startups across the 20 sectoral categories and the two startup-focused special categories will be eligible for a cash prize of ₹25 lakh per category, subject to the applicable award guidelines. Workshop on Base Revision of State -level Index of Industrial Production during 28–30 October 2026 at Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) is convening a three Days Workshop on Base Revision of State-level Index of Industrial Production (IIP), at Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam in collaboration with Department of Economics and Statistics (DES), Keralam during 28–30 October 2026.
The IIP is a key indicator of industrial performance, tracking changes in performance of industrial sector in economy. It is widely used by policymakers, economists, businesses and investors to assess trends in industrial activity and support informed decision-making. The index also serves as an important input in estimating overall economic growth.
MoSPI has updated the base year of the All-India IIP from 2011-12 to 2022-23. The base year is the reference year against which changes in production in later years are measured. A more recent base year helps the index reflect what India’s industries actually produce at present. The revised series incorporates several methodological improvements, including revision of the item basket and weights, updating of the factory panel, expansion of coverage to include activities such as Gas Supply, Water Supply, Sewerage and Waste Management and provision for factory substitution.
The State DES are responsible for compiling and disseminating the State-level IIP. As the nodal Ministry at the national level, the MoSPI provides technical guidance to States and Union Territories (UTs) to promote methodological uniformity and improve the quality and comparability of industrial statistics.
The three-day workshop will familiarise participating States and UTs with the proposed changes in the structure and methods of the revised IIP and help them finalise the list of items to be tracked and the factories that will report data. It will also provide a platform for discussions and feedback on the revisions to National Industrial Classification-2025 and National Product Classification.
Around 60 officials from MoSPI and the DESs of various States and UTs are expected to take part. Through this workshop, MoSPI aims to strengthen the quality, consistency and comparability of industrial statistics across the country.

It is widely used by policymakers, economists, businesses and investors to assess trends in industrial activity and support informed decision-making.

India’s Genetic Diversity Could Make It a Global Destination for Gene Research: Dr. Jitendra Singh
articles.full_content:
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh addresses Session on System and Synthetic Biology at ESTIC 2026, stressing India’s potential in gene research and biotechnology India’s diverse genetic and phenotypic profile offers significant opportunities for scientific research and healthcare innovation Focus on developing domestic gene-synthesis capabilities and strengthening India’s biotechnology ecosystem: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, has said that India’s rich genetic diversity holds significant potential to make the country an important global resource for gene research, with other nations looking towards India for its unique genetic resources in the coming years.
Addressing a session on System and Synthetic Biology at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised the need to build domestic capabilities in emerging areas of biotechnology and translate India’s scientific strengths into research opportunities and practical applications.
The Minister said India’s remarkable genetic and phenotypic diversity provides a valuable foundation for research, particularly in understanding variations in disease patterns and exploring new possibilities in healthcare. He expressed confidence that as India develops and scales up its research capabilities, the country can emerge as an important source of genetic resources for the global scientific community.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also stressed the importance of strengthening indigenous technological capabilities in gene synthesis. Dependence on overseas suppliers for specialised research requirements can create challenges for Indian scientists in terms of time, access and research continuity. Building domestic capabilities in this area would help researchers pursue their work more efficiently and strengthen the country’s biotechnology ecosystem.
The Minister said India has considerable scientific talent and that the government has accorded high priority to research and innovation. He emphasised the need to strengthen the support systems required to take research forward, including greater industry participation and funding for promising scientific work.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also spoke about the growing convergence of disciplines and the need to bring together biology, engineering, mathematics and other areas of expertise. Such interdisciplinary collaboration is becoming increasingly important as scientific research moves towards more complex applications and new technology pathways.

Traditional craftsmanship takes centre stage at the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum at Parliament House Complex, New Delhi
Artisans and craftspeople under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme of the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises participated at the two-day Cultural Bazar organised during the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum at the Parliament House Complex, New Delhi, on 26–27 October 2026.
The Cultural Bazar provided a platform to showcase India’s rich cultural heritage, traditional crafts, artisan-made products and indigenous skills to national and international delegates attending the BRICS Parliamentary Forum. The participation highlighted the diversity of India’s traditional craftsmanship and the contribution of artisan communities to preserving the country’s cultural legacy. BRICS delegates also appreciated the products made by Vishwakarmas.
• Eight PM Vishwakarma artisans and craftspeople from Rajasthan, Jammu and Kashmir, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Nagaland, Karnataka and Maharashtra participated in the Cultural Bazar, showcasing India’s diverse traditional craftsmanship.
• Representing traditional trades such as Tailor, Goldsmith, Sculptor/Stone Carver, Doll and Toy Maker, and Cobbler, the artisans displayed their handcrafted products at the PM Vishwakarma stall. Selected artisans also conducted live demonstrations of traditional craft-making techniques, offering visitors an opportunity to witness the skills and craftsmanship involved in creating these products.
• The participation provided a valuable platform to enhance the visibility and recognition of traditional artisans, expand market exposure and highlight the impact of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme in preserving traditional skills and empowering artisan communities.

Through the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, he participated in exhibitions, including Dilli Haat and the State Trade Fair, gaining wider market exposure. His onboarding on Amazon has further opened opportunities to expand his customer base and strengthen his livelihood.

Practising the GI-tagged Jabalpur Stone Craft, he combines traditional artistry with intricate detailing. articles.full_content:

Shri M. Thennarasan, Principal Secretary, Urban Development and Urban Housing Department, Government of Gujarat, expressed the state government’s commitment to the effective implementation of the ‘Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026’ across Gujarat. He was speaking at a special press conference organized by the Urban Development and Urban Housing Department, Government of Gujarat, in collaboration with the Press Information Bureau (PIB), in Gandhinagar.
He stated, “Cleanliness is not merely a government scheme; it is a way of life. We hope that, with the support of the media, this campaign reaches every individual and that everyone embraces cleanliness as their own responsibility, contributing to this government initiative.” He noted that the Hon’ble Prime Minister and the Hon’ble Chief Minister have placed special emphasis on health and sanitation, and significant budgetary allocations have been made to support these efforts. Furthermore, under the guidance of the Urban Development and Urban Housing Department, comprehensive planning has been undertaken across the state to ensure cleanliness and the scientific disposal of waste.
During the conference, detailed information was provided on the ‘Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026’, which came into effect on April 1, 2026, to realise the Government of Gujarat’s vision of a “Clean Gujarat, Healthy Gujarat” (Swachh Gujarat, Swasth Gujarat).
Smt. Remya Mohan, Secretary (Housing and Urban Development); Shri Sidharth Bodke, ADG, PIB Gujarat; and Ms.Pushpa Lata, Mission Director, Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban were also present at the press conference.
Smt. Remya Mohan stated that the cleanliness mission is a continuous process. She further explained that the ‘Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026’ provide a framework for determining the future course of action and establishing a roadmap to realise the vision of a ‘Swachh Bharat’.
Ms. Pushpa Lata, Mission Director, Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban, provided detailed information on the key provisions and new guidelines under the ‘Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026’. She outlined the four categories of waste segregation: wet waste, dry waste, sanitary waste, and waste requiring special handling, including biomedical and hazardous waste. She also provided information on the prescribed procedures for waste collection, management, and scientific disposal.

articles.full_content:
The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) undertook a review of cleanliness in its office sections and the status of file disposal under Special Campaign 6, aimed at institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency in government offices.
On 26th October 2026, Shri Aditya Pratap Singh, Director, MNRE, accompanied by Shri Rajat Yadav, Under Secretary, inspected various sections of the Ministry at Atal Akshaya Urja Bhawan, Lodhi Road, New Delhi.
During the inspection, the officers reviewed the maintenance and organisation of office spaces and emphasised the need to ensure cleanliness and proper utilisation of available space. The status of file disposal was also reviewed, with emphasis on the timely processing of files and expeditious clearance of pending cases.
The review reiterated the importance of regular monitoring, efficient file management and the active participation of officers and staff in achieving the objectives of Special Campaign 6. MNRE remains committed to promoting Swachhata, improving workplace organisation and reducing pendency through sustained efforts and effective administrative practices.

Department of Commerce Extends RELIEF Initiative under Export Promotion Mission Until March 31, 2027
articles.full_content:
RELIEF Component II Offers 95% Risk Coverage to Encourage ECGC Cover for Export Shipments
The Department of Commerce has extended the timelines under Component II of RELIEF (Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation), a time-bound intervention under the Export Promotion Mission (EPM), until March 31, 2027. The extension was notified vide Notification No. 37/2026-27 dated September 30, 2026, in view of continued geopolitical disruptions in West Asia and their impact on maritime logistics across the Gulf and adjoining regions.
Component II of the initiative aims to encourage exporters to obtain Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (ECGC) cover for upcoming shipments to specified regions by providing 95 per cent risk coverage. The benefit is available for Standalone Policies and Whole Turnover Policies obtained on or after March 16, 2026. Under this component, the premium payable by eligible exporters is protected against increases beyond pre-disruption levels during the eligible period. The covered cargo categories include Full Container Load (FCL), Less than Container Load (LCL) and refrigerated (reefer) containers, excluding energy shipments.
Exporters seeking coverage under the RELIEF initiative are required to submit claims and supporting documents through the ECGC customer portal at www.ecgcltd.in . Guidance on generating user IDs and passwords, completing exporter registration and submitting claims under the initiative is available through dedicated video tutorials on ECGC’s official YouTube channel, @ecgcltd7016.
Launched on March 19, 2026, RELIEF is a targeted intervention to support Indian exporters facing extraordinary freight cost escalation, higher insurance premia and war-related export risks arising from disruptions in the Gulf and the wider West Asian maritime corridor.
The extension of RELIEF underscores the Government’s commitment to strengthening export resilience, sustaining trade flows and supporting Indian exporters amid continuing geopolitical and maritime logistics uncertainties.
C N Abhijith Narayanan/ Abhimanyu Panwar
